text:
The ringing failure most likely comes from **Cc**, the Miller compensation capacitor, being set far too small.

- **Only stability fails.** DC accuracy, line regulation and quiescent current all pass. The only failure is 0.70 V peak-to-peak ringing that is still present 7–10 µs after each load step, so the loop is nearly unstable.
- **Cc is implausibly small.** It is 35 fF. It is connected between the gate of a very large pass device (Mp, W = 347.6 µm) and the output, which carries a 1 nF load. Miller compensation of an LDO with this load needs roughly 1–10 pF to split the poles. At 35 fF the capacitor does almost nothing, so the error-amp pole at node g and the output pole sit too close together. The result is little phase margin and a ringing output.
- **The M5 triode flag is not the fault.** The tail node sits at 0.025 V because Vref is 0.6 V and M1/M2 need about 0.575 V of Vgs. That comes from the topology itself. The bias currents still look normal: about 12.9 µA in the tail and 6.4 µA per branch.
- **Mp, M1 and R1/R2 are weaker candidates.** They are the elements the sensitivity analysis flags, but each shifts ripple by only about 5%. That is far too little to explain a 70× violation.
